Alex / Priya — great to meet today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our perf/SLO discovery: 

Key SLOs you called out
- 95th percentile token latency target: <= 150ms (for streaming responses)
- Average end-to-end response time goal: ~300ms for typical 1-2k token responses (streaming preferred)
- Sustained throughput: ~200 QPS (peaks to 400 QPS expected during promos)
- Concurrency target: ~50 concurrent interactive sessions
- Availability: 99.9% plus graceful fallback to smaller models if capacity constrained

Primary constraints / ask from your side
- Streaming is required (client-side UX pipes immediate tokens)
- Tight tail latency for 95/99 percentiles matters more than raw throughput
- Cost target: minimize $/response without regressions in quality for customer-facing chat

Cost / performance levers we discussed (high-level)
- Continuous batching: lowers per-token compute by grouping concurrent in-flight requests; helps with high-throughput peaks without raising base latency for single users
- Prefix / KV caching: cache warm prefixes (prompts, system instantiation) to shave repeated decode costs for common flows
- Quantization profiles: int8 / mixed-precision options to reduce GPU memory and increase concurrency — good fit for less-sensitive prompts or background ranking calls
- Model variants: route critical interactive sessions to higher-quality variants (fp16 13B) and lower-cost variants (quantized 7B) for lower-value paths or fallbacks
- Autoscaling + warm pools: maintain a small warm reserve to avoid cold-start tail spikes during promo bursts

Next steps / owners
1) Priyom (cc'd) to run a quick sizing exercise (I attached redwood_performance_grid.xlsx) and propose an initial cluster footprint and cost delta vs current targets — action: Priyom, by Fri 2026-03-24
2) Technical deep-dive to validate streaming chunking, KV cache behavior, and tail-latency mitigations — propose 60-minute call next week (see link in related_links) — owner: Marissa to schedule
3) Deliver mutual action plan (MAP) draft with milestones for pilot, perf validation, and rollout — attached: nova_mutual_action_plan.docx — owner: Marissa / Alex to align on dates

Please let me know if I misunderstood any of the targets. If this aligns, I'll have Priyom send a tech note with sizing and propose time windows for next-week deep-dive.

Alex — great questions. Quick technical clarifications / notes below (happy to expand on the deep-dive):

Streaming chunking vs per-token flush
- Recommended: 50–100ms flush window for most UIs. Per-token flush increases network overhead & can amplify tail noise; 50–100ms batching of tokens gives smooth UX while keeping tail latency within your 150ms 95th target in practice.

KV cache warmup and first-response behavior
- KV cache is per-prefix (system + few-shot examples) and is warmed after the first request for a given prompt pattern. For new sessions we expect initial request to pay the full model compute; subsequent requests with the same prefix are significantly cheaper (lower latency).
- Mitigation: prewarming popular system prompts at the edge (warm pool) reduces first-request penalty for new sessions by keeping a cached KV snapshot. We can include an estimate in the sizing spreadsheet for the warm-pool cost vs latency benefit.

Tail-latency controls
- Maintain small warm reserve replica pool to absorb spikes (reduces queueing).
- Prefer continuous batching with a small max-delay (5–10ms) for low-latency tiers and larger pack windows for background/async workloads.
- Quantized kernels (int8) add slight variance to per-token time but usually reduce cost meaningfully; for tail-sensitive interactive sessions we recommend fp16 13B and int8 7B for lower-cost paths and fallback routing.

Rough cost order-of-magnitude (ballpark; see redwood_performance_grid.xlsx for details)
- 13B fp16 (optimized): baseline unit cost X per 1k messages (higher quality, lower latency)
- 7B int8 (quantized): ~35–55% lower $/response depending on batch sizes and effective concurrency
- Continuous batching + caching: combined can reduce effective $/response by another ~20–35% on repeat flows

Deliverables I will prepare by Fri (2026-03-24)
- Cluster footprint & warm-pool sizing (spreadsheet tab)
- Per-variant $/1k messages estimates (13B fp16 vs 7B int8) with assumptions (avg tokens, batching, cache hit-rate)
- Short note on expected 95/99 tail latency under proposed config and recommended guardrails for autoscaling
